issue.title: Bug: `MutableScopeHeaders.__setitem__` fails when replacing 3+ duplicate headers (IndexError / drops wrong headers)

labels.name: repo-4f281e34
labels.description: This is something that is not working as expected

issue.body:
### Description

When an ASGI message contains 3 or more headers with the same key, assigning a new value to that key via `MutableScopeHeaders[key] = value` fails.

Depending on the header list layout, this either raises an `IndexError` or removes unrelated headers while leaving stale duplicates behind. Because `__setitem__` is documented to overwrite existing entries, it should consolidate them into a single header entry while leaving all other headers intact.

### Root Cause

In `litestar/datastructures/headers.py` (`MutableScopeHeaders.__setitem__`), duplicate entries are removed by iterating through their indices in ascending order:

```python
del self.headers[i]
```

Because the underlying list shrinks on each deletion, the remaining indices shift, causing subsequent `del` operations to target the wrong index or go out of bounds.

### Reproducible Example (IndexError)

```python
from litestar.datastructures import MutableScopeHeaders

message = {
    "type": "http.response.start",
    "status": 200,
    "headers": [
        (b"cache-control", b"private"),
        (b"cache-control", b"max-age=0"),
        (b"cache-control", b"must-revalidate"),
    ],
}

headers = MutableScopeHeaders.from_message(message)
headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"

assert message["headers"] == [(b"cache-control", b"no-store")]
```

**Traceback:**

```text
  File "litestar/datastructures/headers.py", line 214, in __setitem__
    del self.headers[i]
IndexError: list assignment index out of range
```

### Reproducible Example (Wrong Header Removed)

If extra headers follow the duplicates, the shifted index removes the wrong header:

```python
from litestar.datastructures import MutableScopeHeaders

message = {
    "type": "http.response.start",
    "status": 200,
    "headers": [
        (b"cache-control", b"private"),
        (b"cache-control", b"max-age=0"),
        (b"cache-control", b"must-revalidate"),
        (b"content-type", b"text/plain"),
        (b"x-marker", b"tail"),
    ],
}

headers = MutableScopeHeaders.from_message(message)
headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"

# Expected:
# [
#     (b"cache-control", b"no-store"),
#     (b"content-type", b"text/plain"),
#     (b"x-marker", b"tail"),
# ]
#
# Actual:
# [
#     (b"cache-control", b"no-store"),
#     (b"cache-control", b"must-revalidate"),  # Old duplicate retained
#     (b"x-marker", b"tail"),  # content-type was incorrectly deleted
# ]
```

### Additional Context

- Iterating over `reversed(indices[1:])` would remove the extra occurrences without invalidating the remaining indices.
- PR [#4927](https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar/pull/4927) addresses duplicate values in `extend_header_value()`, but its reviewed patch does not change the deletion loop in `__setitem__`.


### URL to code causing the issue

_No response_

### MCVE

```python

```

### Steps to reproduce

Run either of the standalone examples in the description. The first raises IndexError; the second removes content-type and retains an old cache-control entry.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Logs

```text

```

### Litestar Version

3.0.0b0 (commit 574e436d2a629a1a8775ea0bed11091a80f50703)

### Platform

- [ ] Linux
- [ ] Mac
- [x] Windows
- [ ] Other (Please specify in the description above)

It includes regression tests for three duplicate headers and preservation of unrelated headers, plus a changelog entry. `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_datastructures/test_headers.py -q` passes (75 tests), and Ruff check/format checks pass. issue.title: [Bug]: image_histogram2d(None) raises AttributeError instead of TypeError
issue.body:
### What happened?

`image_histogram2d` accepts a tensor image, but when passed `None` it raises an incidental `AttributeError` while checking the image rank, instead of the `TypeError` used for other non-tensor inputs. This makes invalid input handling inconsistent and hides the function's actual input contract.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
from kornia.enhance import image_histogram2d

image_histogram2d(None)
# AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'dim'
```

A string input raises `TypeError` from the existing type check, while `None` bypasses that check and reaches `_check_image_rank`.

### Environment

- Kornia version: 0.9.1.dev
- PyTorch version: 2.15.0+cpu
- Python version: 3.11.9
- OS / device (CPU, CUDA, ROCm, MPS): Windows / CPU

### Anything else?

This was reproduced on the current checkout. The fix should validate every non-tensor input, including `None`, before checking the image rank and pin the exception in a regression test.

issue.title: `st.date_input` accepts reversed date ranges from query parameters

labels.name: repo-ebbaa65b
labels.description: Bug has been confirmed by the Streamlit team

labels.name: repo-ebbaa65b
labels.description: Medium priority - worth fixing without urgency

issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce the problem.

### Summary

When `st.date_input` is used in range mode with `bind="query-params"`, a URL containing two valid dates in reverse order is accepted as-is. The widget returns the end date before the start date, despite the date range being invalid.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from datetime import date
import streamlit as st

st.date_input(
    "Date range",
    value=(date(2025, 3, 1), date(2025, 3, 15)),
    key="period",
    bind="query-params",
)
```

Open the app with the `period` query parameter containing `2025-03-15` followed by `2025-03-01` (for example, `?period=2025-03-15&period=2025-03-01`).

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the example above.
2. Open the app with `period` set to two in-bounds date values in descending order.
3. Read the value returned by `st.date_input`.

### Expected Behavior

Invalid reversed query-parameter ranges should not be exposed as a reversed date range. The widget should reject the malformed range and fall back to its configured default, consistent with how it handles invalid and out-of-bounds query-parameter values.

### Current Behavior

`DateInputSerde.deserialize` parses both dates and returns them in the original order. It validates that the dates are individually within bounds, but does not check that the start date is less than or equal to the end date.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: Current `develop` checkout
- Python version: Not verified
- Operating System: Not verified
- Browser: Not verified

### Additional Information

The existing date-input serde tests cover ordered ranges and out-of-bounds values, but not reversed ranges.

issue.title: Bug: More-specific q=0 media range is overridden by wildcard Accept range
issue.body:
### Description

A broad wildcard range with a positive quality value can override a more-specific media range that explicitly sets `q=0`. Under Accept negotiation, the more-specific media range determines the quality for a matching representation, so the exact `text/html;q=0` range should make `text/html` unacceptable despite `text/*;q=1`.

This is related to #5072, but the wildcard fallback is a distinct case: simply skipping zero-quality entries still allows the broad range to select the explicitly excluded representation.

### URL to code causing the issue

https://github.com/litestar-org/litestar/blob/main/litestar/datastructures/headers.py

### MCVE

from litestar.datastructures import Accept

accept = Accept("text/*;q=1,text/html;q=0")
print(accept.best_match(["text/html"]))

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the MCVE with the repository's current code.
2. It returns `text/html`; expected result is `None` because the more-specific range explicitly rejects that representation.

### Screenshots

N/A

### Logs

Actual output: `text/html`
Expected output: `None`

### Litestar Version

3.0.0b0 (current repository checkout)

### Platform

- [ ] Linux
- [ ] Mac
- [x] Windows

issue.title: Reject malformed Docker log timestamps
issue.body:
## What happened

`rgkl` emits a Docker-format log record with a zero-value timestamp when the record's `time` field is not a valid timestamp. `process_output` uses `Timestamp::from_str(time_str).unwrap_or_default()`, so a parse error becomes the Unix epoch instead of rejecting the malformed record.

## What you expected

Malformed Docker log records should not be emitted with a fabricated timestamp. Match the CRI parser's behavior and skip the record when its timestamp cannot be parsed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Process a Docker-format log line such as `{"log":"example\n","stream":"stdout","time":"not-a-timestamp"}` through the agent's log reader.
2. Observe that it produces a record timestamped at the zero value (Unix epoch).

## Environment

- **Kubetail version:** Current development version
- **Install method:** Cluster Agent reading Docker-format container logs
- **OS + arch:** Linux node; architecture not confirmed
- **Cluster:** Kubernetes cluster using Docker-format container logs

issue.title: [BUG] Text.right_crop with a negative amount corrupts text length
issue.body:
- [x] I've checked [docs](https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html) and searched open and closed issues for possible solutions.
- [x] I can't find my issue in the [FAQ](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/blob/master/FAQ.md).

<!-- 
WAIT! Is this a feature request?

Rich isn't accepting new features. If it can be implemented in a third-party library, then that is what I recommend.

Rich *may* accept enhancements to existing features, if they don't have a disruptive impact on the API.

If you think your feature is exceptional, then please make your case in a discussion.
-->

**Describe the bug**

`Text.right_crop()` behaves unexpectedly for a negative `amount`: it removes characters from the *start* of the text while increasing the cached length, leaving the `Text` object internally inconsistent.

Minimal reproduction:

```python
from rich.text import Text

text = Text(abc)
text.right_crop(-1)
print(repr(text.plain), len(text))
```

Observed output:

```text
'a' 4
```

A value of `-4` leaves `plain == abc` but reports `len(text) == 7`. The implementation calculates `self.plain[:-amount]` and subtracts `amount` from the cached length, so negative values both slice from the wrong end and increase the cached length. Subsequent operations that rely on the cached length or span offsets can then behave incorrectly.

Expected behavior: a negative crop amount should not silently mutate the text or invalidate its length/spans. Rejecting negative values with `ValueError` would make the invalid input explicit; please advise if a different contract is preferred.

This report and reproduction were prepared with GitHub Copilot assistance; the example was run locally against the current checkout.

**Platform**
<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

Windows, PowerShell. The behavior is in `Text`'s internal string/length bookkeeping and does not depend on terminal rendering.

</details>

comment.body:
I reproduced this locally and prepared a narrow fix: `Text.right_crop()` raises `ValueError` for a negative amount before changing the text, cached length, or spans. Regression tests cover `-1` and `-4`; `python -m pytest tests/test_text.py -q` passes (115 tests).

This change was prepared with GitHub Copilot assistance. @willmcgugan, does rejecting negative amounts with `ValueError` match the intended API behavior? Per `AI_POLICY.md`, I will wait for your approval before opening an AI-assisted pull request.

issue.title: [BUG] get_pages_showing_field crashes for a widget pointing to an orphan page

labels.name: repo-64630712
labels.description: From a users perspective, this is about robustness

issue.body:
`get_pages_showing_field()` raises an uncaught `TypeError` when a widget's `/P` entry points to a page dictionary that is not present in the document's page tree. In non-strict mode, `_get_page_number_by_indirect()` returns `None`, which is then used as a sequence index instead of ignoring the malformed widget or raising a PDF-specific error.

## Environment

```bash
$ python -m platform
Windows-10-10.0.26200-SP0

$ python -c "import pypdf;print(pypdf._debug_versions)"
pypdf 7.0.0 (Python 3.11.9, Windows)
```

## Code + PDF

This example creates a one-page PDF with a form widget whose `/P` points to an orphan page dictionary, then reads the field back. The malformed input is generated in memory; no separate PDF file is needed.

```python
from io import BytesIO
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
from pypdf.generic import ArrayObject, DictionaryObject, NameObject, TextStringObject

writer = PdfWriter()
writer.add_blank_page(width=72, height=72)
orphan_page = DictionaryObject({
    NameObject("/Type"): NameObject("/Page"),
    NameObject("/MediaBox"): ArrayObject(),
})
orphan_ref = writer._add_object(orphan_page)
widget = DictionaryObject({
    NameObject("/FT"): NameObject("/Tx"),
    NameObject("/T"): TextStringObject("field"),
    NameObject("/Subtype"): NameObject("/Widget"),
    NameObject("/P"): orphan_ref,
})
widget_ref = writer._add_object(widget)
acroform = DictionaryObject({NameObject("/Fields"): ArrayObject([widget_ref])})
writer.root_object[NameObject("/AcroForm")] = writer._add_object(acroform)

stream = BytesIO()
writer.write(stream)
stream.seek(0)
reader = PdfReader(stream, strict=False)
field = reader.root_object["/AcroForm"]["/Fields"][0]
reader.get_pages_showing_field(field)
```

## Traceback

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 18, in <module>
  File "pypdf/_doc_common.py", line 972, in get_pages_showing_field
    return [
  File "pypdf/_doc_common.py", line 975, in <listcomp>
    else (self.pages[self._get_page_number_by_indirect(x.indirect_reference)])
  File "pypdf/_page.py", line 2521, in __getitem__
    raise TypeError("Sequence indices must be integers")
TypeError: Sequence indices must be integers
```

issue.title: [Bug] save_to_html cannot clear the widget Mapbox token
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
`KeplerGl.save_to_html()` cannot clear a Mapbox token configured on the widget. The method uses an empty string as its default and treats any empty value as "inherit the widget token," so explicitly passing `mapbox_token=""` still embeds the stored token in the exported HTML.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a widget with a token: `widget = KeplerGl(mapbox_token="pk.widget_token")`.
2. Export with `widget.save_to_html(file_name="map.html", mapbox_token="")`.
3. Inspect the exported HTML: it still contains `pk.widget_token` in `MAPBOX_TOKEN`.

**Expected behavior**
Omitting `mapbox_token` should inherit the widget's configured token. Explicitly passing an empty string should clear it so a token-free basemap can be used.

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
- OS: N/A (Python API behavior)
- Browser: N/A
- Version: keplergl 0.4.0 source

**Smartphone (please complete the following information):**
- Device: N/A
- OS: N/A
- Browser: N/A
- Version: N/A

**Additional context**
The `save_to_html()` docstring says to leave the token empty for free MapLibre styles, but the current fallback makes that impossible when the widget was initialized with a token.

issue.title: [BUG] fill_missing_values auto leaves all-NaN series unchanged
issue.body:
*Info: All issues must be approved by a maintainer (labeled **`ok`**) before opening pull requests. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md).*

**Describe the bug**
`fill_missing_values(series, fill=auto)` silently returns an all-NaN series unchanged. The function documentation says it returns a series with all missing values filled, but interpolation cannot infer values when a component has no non-missing observations.

**To Reproduce**
```python
import numpy as np
from darts import TimeSeries
from darts.utils.missing_values import fill_missing_values

series = TimeSeries.from_values(np.full(3, np.nan))
filled = fill_missing_values(series, fill=auto)
print(np.isnan(filled.values()).any())  # True
```

**Expected behavior**
The helper should not silently report success while returning missing values. For an all-NaN component, it should raise a clear error explaining that automatic interpolation cannot fill it, or clearly document the unchanged result.

**System (please complete the following information):**
 - Python version: 3.11
 - darts version: master (0.48.1)

**Additional context**
`darts.utils.missing_values._auto_fill()` delegates to `DataFrame.interpolate(limit_direction=both)`; an all-NaN column remains all NaN after interpolation. This is distinct from filling leading/trailing gaps in a series that has valid observations.
